title: 15-Minute Beef and Broccoli Stir Fry That Beats the Delivery Fee
description: Skip the $38 takeout bill. This easy beef and broccoli stir fry takes 15 minutes in one hot skillet with tender flank steak and a glossy savory sauce.
storyHeading: Why This Saved My Tuesday Night
story: By 6:30 PM on a rain-soaked Tuesday, staring down a $41 DoorDash cart for two soggy cartons of takeout felt like personal defeat. I shut my phone, pulled a pound of flank steak from the meat drawer, and timed myself. Fourteen minutes later, I had crisp-tender florets and glossy, seared beef sizzling on the stove. My early testing failure with this dish was crowding the skillet—dumping raw beef and cold broccoli in together turns everything into a grey, watery stew. Searing the beef in a screaming-hot pan first, pulling it out while it is still slightly pink, and then using two tablespoons of water to steam-fry the broccoli in the residual drippings is the entire secret. It gives you that blistered restaurant texture without an industrial jet burner.
ingredients: 1 lb flank steak, sliced thinly across the grain
4 cups fresh broccoli florets, cut into small bite-sized pieces
2 tbsp avocado oil or vegetable oil, divided
instructions: Whisk the soy sauce, beef broth, brown sugar, cornstarch, minced garlic, and grated ginger in a measuring cup until the starch completely dissolves.

Set a 12-inch heavy skillet over high heat with 1 tablespoon of oil until shimmering, then lay the sliced beef flat in a single layer and sear undisturbed for 90 seconds until charred on the edges before flipping for 30 seconds and transferring immediately to a plate.

Pour the remaining oil and broccoli florets into the hot pan, stir for 1 minute, splash in 2 tablespoons of water, and immediately slap a lid on top to steam for 2 minutes until tender-crisp and bright green.
Pull the lid off, tip the beef and resting juices back in, pour over the sauce mixture, and toss over medium-high heat for 60 seconds until the sauce bubbles up thick and glossy.
proHack: Pop your flank steak into the freezer for 15 minutes before cooking. Chilling the meat firms up the muscle fibers, making it easy to slice paper-thin, tender strips with zero ragged tearing.
servingIdea: Pile over quick microwaved Jasmine rice or toss directly with cooked ramen noodles, finished with sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds.
storage: Store in an airtight glass container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot skillet with a teaspoon of oil for 2 minutes to keep the broccoli snappy instead of rubbery.

faqs.question: Can I swap the flank steak for ground beef or chicken?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Lean ground beef works great—brown it first, drain excess grease, and follow the remaining steps. Boneless chicken thighs sliced thin cook on the exact same timeline.

faqs.question: How do I make sure my sauce actually thickens?
faqs.answer: Ensure your skillet is hot and the sauce reaches a full rolling bubble. Cornstarch requires a temperature of roughly 203°F to activate and create that shiny, clingy sauce.
